title: Why one third is bigger than one quarter
examples: Why is a bigger bottom number a smaller fraction?

explain.say: Would you rather share a pizza with 2 friends or with 3 friends? Look at the bars: the top one is cut into 3 equal parts, the bottom one into 4. One third is shaded on top, one quarter below. Which piece is longer?

draw.text: Why one third is bigger than one quarter

explain.say: One third is longer! Sharing among 3 gives bigger pieces than sharing among 4. So a bigger bottom number means smaller pieces, and one quarter is smaller. Is that a surprise?
See how fast the pieces shrink. One half is huge, but one eighth is tiny: you need 8 of them to fill the bar. Which would you choose for dessert?
When both top numbers are 1, just look at the bottom. One fifth beats one tenth, because 5 parts are bigger than 10 parts. Which is bigger: one sixth or one twelfth?

Well done! On a pie it is just as clear: one third is a bigger slice than one quarter. A famous story from the USA: a third-pound burger did not sell, because many people thought a quarter was bigger! Now you know better.

faq.a: Yes. One third is one of 3 equal parts, and one quarter is one of 4 equal parts. Fewer parts means each part is bigger.
asks: Which is bigger, a third or a quarter?

faq.q: Why is a bigger bottom number a smaller fraction?
faq.a: The bottom number tells you how many equal parts the whole is cut into. The more parts you cut, the smaller each one must be.
One fifth is bigger. Cutting into 5 parts makes bigger pieces than cutting into 8.
asks: Is one fifth bigger than one eighth?

faq.a: A unit fraction has 1 on top, like one half, one third or one quarter. It means just one of the equal parts.

faq.q: Does this rule work for 2/3 and 2/5?
faq.a: Yes, when the top numbers are the same. 2 thirds is bigger than 2 fifths, because each third is bigger than each fifth.
asks: What if both top numbers are 2?

facts: When two fractions have the same top number, the one with the smaller bottom number is bigger.

quiz.why: One half has the fewest parts, so its piece is the biggest.

wrong.0: 1/6 is cut into more parts than 1/2, so it is smaller.
wrong.1: 1/10 is cut into the most parts, so it is the smallest.

quiz.say: Two same-sized pizzas: pizza A is shared by 3 people, pizza B by 6. Who gets more?
quiz.show: Two same-sized pizzas: pizza A is shared by 3 people, pizza B by 6. Who gets more?
quiz.why: One third is bigger than one sixth, so each person sharing pizza A gets more.

wrong.1: 6 people share pizza B, so each gets a smaller piece.
wrong.2: One third and one sixth are not the same size.
